Bringing a quiet clinic page back to life

I restarted regular posting for a dental and aesthetic clinic, planned the content and worked through a careful approval process.

My role

I researched the market, planned the posts, wrote captions, managed publishing and replies, and helped direct the videos.

Sector

Healthcare · Dental & aesthetic clinic

Status

Case study / reported evidence

Topics

Healthcare · Approval systems · Video content

01 / Starting point

The challenge

The clinic’s pages had been inactive for nearly a year. The content covered dental and aesthetic treatments, so every post needed extra care and sign-off before publication.

The insight

When a business works in a sensitive field, it is better to plan approvals in advance than rush content through at the last minute.

02 / The approach

The plan

  • Look at how other dental and aesthetic clinics explain their services.
  • Plan different post formats for the clinic’s two service areas.
  • Leave time for reviews and approvals before scheduling anything.
03 / Execution

Make the rhythm visible.

Research

I looked at local and international clinic content before deciding on the topics and tone.

Video content

I helped create a doctor introduction video that included a client testimonial. We then used the same format for two more videos.

Approvals

One offer needed four rounds of feedback. I kept track of the changes and waited for sign-off before publishing.

06 / Selected proof

A closer look at the work.

These examples include dates and sources so you can see what they show and what they do not.

04 / Results

Evidence with the label still attached.

The supplied report shows 16,854 organic Instagram views, around 2,600 accounts reached and 222 interactions between 6 November and 3 December 2025. Facebook recorded 937 views and 254 viewers. These figures do not tell us how many patients booked an appointment.

05 / Reflection

What stays after the campaign?

The most useful lesson was to plan enough time for reviews. Even with several rounds of changes, we could keep the content moving without ignoring important approvals.

Credits
My contribution: research, content calendar, captions, video direction, publishing and community management. Client identity withheld.
